record.tranche_reason: Applies mechanistic interpretation of modular-addition networks to a one-hidden-layer MLP and reports its learned algorithm; it does not test grokking timing.
record.gate_note: Reports final train/validation accuracy, a cosine-based interpretation of learned weights, weight replacements, and evaluations of randomly specified cosine neurons. It does not report numerical accuracy curves or describe a delayed test-accuracy rise. The comparison to Transformer results is discussed in the text, but those earlier results are not recorded as this study's rows.
record.test_reason: It interprets the algorithm a one-hidden-layer MLP learns for modular addition and contrasts it with the Transformer algorithm. That bears on V6, whether different architectures converge on the same algorithm. It does not test grokking timing (V1, V2) or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. One-hidden-layer MLPs learn modular addition with cosine-patterned neurons whose input and output frequencies match and whose phases add. Unlike the Transformer, they seem to favour, and probably need, a broad range of frequencies.
record.recipe_differences: The post analyzes a one-hidden-layer MLP with one-hot inputs and outputs, rather than the one-layer Transformer discussed in the cited work. It fits cosine functions to weights and tests weight replacements and randomly specified cosine neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The author says the hyperparameters were not tuned much and that robustness to other hyperparameters is suspected but not tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing over 90% of neurons with cosine fits keeps accuracy above 80%. Random cosine neurons reach over 95% accuracy with 256 neurons and perfect accuracy with 512.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The cosine-neuron algorithm is a sufficient mechanism for modular addition in one-hot MLPs.

record.problems: No numerical accuracy values or uncertainty estimates are reported for the trained MLP. The text does not describe the timing of accuracy changes, and the author notes that hyperparameter robustness was suspected but not tested.

untested.parts: Timing of the test-accuracy rise relative to training accuracy, and how the delay depends on training-set size. The curves are shown but not described.
Gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, and progress measures.
Non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweeps, and weight-norm interventions.
Varying weight decay, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Repeated runs of the same architecture, hyperparameter variation, and a direct side-by-side training of a Transformer.

missing.what: Training/validation accuracy and loss curves over epochs (log x-axis), which could show whether generalization was delayed. The text gives no values.

record.verdict_notes: An informal LessWrong post with a single run and no uncertainty estimates; hyperparameter robustness was not tested. The V6 evidence is a qualitative contrast with prior work, not a controlled comparison. It is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether training accuracy saturates while test accuracy stays at chance, whether test accuracy rises much later, and whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The study analyzes the trained circuit, but does not track gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, continuous progress measures, or whether those measures anticipate a jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm intervention is tested.
No LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning is studied.
Weight decay is used, but its effect is not varied or tested; no efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking is tested.
The post compares its MLP interpretation with the cited Transformer account, but does not compare repeated runs, multiple MLP architectures, or hyperparameter settings.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact is tested.
